newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat's Romiti sticks by June '98 retirement.
newsitem.headline: Fiat's Romiti sticks by June '98 retirement.

text.p: Chairman of Italy's Fiat Cesare Romiti said on Monday that he stuck by his plan to retire as head of the industrial group in June 1998 when he turned 75.
He told a news conference following the group's annual shareholders' meeting, "I have nothing to add to what I said at the shareholders' meeting last year."

Last year, Romiti told shareholders he would step down by June 24, 1998 which will be his 75th birthday. Gianni Agnelli bowed out after 30 years as Chairman in February 1996 ahead of his 75th birthday in March, in accordance with Fiat rules on the retirement of directors.
Romiti declined to answer questions on who his successor as Chairman might be.
He said that when he received a suspended sentence on charges on false accounting earlier this year he had asked Fiat's syndicate of shareholders whether he should resign.

The syndicate of Agnelli holding companies IFI and IFIL, insurer Generali, merchant bank Mediobanca and German banking group Deutsche Bank unaminously asked him not to quit, Romiti said, adding that he therefore had had no intention of thinking of resigning. -- Milan newsroom +39266129502
